request.spec:
When a claim is opened it receives the next number on the sheet: 1 for the first claim ever
opened on the sheet, then 2, and so on, with no gaps and never reused, even when two users open
claims at the same moment. A draft has no number, and voiding a claim clears its number (the
number is not given to anyone else). Show the number on the claim. Every audit line about a
claim that has a number gains number=<number> at its end (so CLAIM_OPENED and CLAIM_SETTLED
carry it; a CLAIM_VOIDED line carries the number the claim had).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When a claim is opened it receives the next number on the sheet: 1 for the first claim ever
opened on the sheet, then 2, and so on, with no gaps and never reused, even when two users open
claims at the same moment. A draft has no number, and voiding a claim clears its number (the
number is not given to anyone else). Show the number on the claim. Every audit line about a
claim that has a number gains number=<number> at its end (so CLAIM_OPENED and CLAIM_SETTLED
carry it; a CLAIM_VOIDED line carries the number the claim had).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims are now numbered when they're opened, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass, including the one where two users open claims at the same moment.

- **Stored data** (`V8__claim_number.sql`): each sheet keeps the last number it handed out, starting at 0. Each claim gets an optional number, and no two claims on a sheet can have the same one.
- **Server**:
  - **Opening a claim:** the app locks the sheet's row while it takes the next number (`SheetService.nextClaimNumber`). Two users opening claims at once get different numbers.
  - **Refused opens:** the number is taken in the same database transaction as the open. If the open is refused, nothing is saved, so no number is used up and there are no gaps.
  - **Voiding** clears the claim's number, and that number is never given out again.
- **Audit**: any line about a claim that has a number ends with ` number=<n>`, so CLAIM_OPENED and CLAIM_SETTLED both carry it. A CLAIM_VOIDED line carries the number the claim had just before it was voided, and a draft's lines have none.
- **Screen**: each claim row shows its number in `claim-number`, which is empty for drafts and voided claims.

Following that same rule, editing a claim that is already open also adds `number=<n>` to its CLAIM_EDITED line. The tests only edit drafts, so they don't cover this case.
